response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT ordersmark, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), s AS (SELECT ordersmark, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orderexecutions) AS share FROM g), d AS (SELECT ordersmark, cnt, share, share - (SELECT AVG(share) FROM s) AS diff FROM s), r AS (SELECT ordersmark, cnt, share, diff, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY diff DESC) AS rnk FROM d) SELECT ordersmark AS order_reference, cnt AS execution_count, share, diff AS share_minus_avg_share FROM r WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY diff DESC

assumptions.assumption: Executions with NULL ordersmark form a single group (GROUP BY puts NULLs together), and that group counts as one order reference row in the average share.
The average share is the unweighted mean over the groups (including the NULL group), computed from the per-group shares.
Ranking is by difference descending using RANK() so ties share a rank and later ranks skip; shares are not rounded.
